title: Balance storage cost and performance, and design durability
learningObjective: Recommend storage that balances features, performance and cost (account types, access tiers, lifecycle management, reservations) and that protects data and keeps it durable (redundancy, immutability, soft delete, versioning, backup).
foundation: Fast storage costs more. Cheap storage is slower or takes time to retrieve. Good design puts each kind of data where it belongs, and moves it automatically as it ages.
Durability means not losing data when hardware, a datacenter or a region fails. Protection means not losing it to mistakes or attackers.
engineer: Performance and cost: Standard general-purpose v2 for most data; Premium block blob (SSD, LRS/ZRS) for low-latency, high-transaction workloads; Premium file shares for IO-intensive shares. Access tiers: Hot, Cool (30-day minimum), Cold (90-day) and Archive (180-day, offline, hours to rehydrate). Lifecycle management rules move or delete data by age or last access; reserved capacity lowers cost for predictable volumes.

Durability: LRS (one datacenter), ZRS (three zones), GRS/RA-GRS (secondary region), GZRS/RA-GZRS (zones plus secondary region). RA- adds read access to the secondary. Customer-managed failover lets you fail over to the secondary. Archive tier supports LRS, GRS and RA-GRS only.

Protection: soft delete for blobs and containers, versioning, point-in-time restore for block blobs, immutable storage (time-based retention and legal hold, at container or version level) for WORM compliance, resource locks against account deletion, Azure Backup for blobs (operational backup within the account, vaulted backup copied to a Backup vault), and object replication for asynchronous copies to another account.

animation.caption: Balance cost and performance, and choose durability and protection features.

example.title: A media company's storage design
body: New uploads are processed from a Premium block blob account; finished assets live in Standard GPv2 Hot and move to Cool after 30 days and Archive after 180 days by lifecycle rules.
Contracts are stored with a 7-year time-based immutability policy on GZRS; vaulted backup protects the asset library against ransomware that could delete the account.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription; most design reviews need only Reader access
permissions: Reader to review existing resources; Contributor or Owner to build the design
limits: Check service limits and regional availability for each component
portal: Storage account > Data management > Lifecycle management: add rules.
Storage account > Data protection: soft delete, versioning, point-in-time restore, immutability.
Backup vault > Backup > Azure Blobs: operational or vaulted backup policy.
configuration.cli:
az storage account management-policy create -g rg-data --account-name stmedia --policy @policy.json
az storage container immutability-policy create -g rg-data --account-name stmedia -c contracts --period 2555

steps: Answer every case in both trainers.
expected: Immutability for WORM; vaulted backup against account deletion

validation.text: Chose the right protection or durability feature

lab.cost: None. The simulation runs entirely in the browser.

troubleshooting.cause: Data moved out of Cool/Cold/Archive before the minimum days.
troubleshooting.fix: Align lifecycle rules with the minimum retention periods.

troubleshooting.symptom: Ransomware encrypted blobs and GRS replicated the damage.
troubleshooting.cause: Redundancy copies changes; it is not backup.
troubleshooting.fix: Enable versioning/soft delete, immutability or vaulted backup.

comparisons.difference: Redundancy survives hardware and site failures; backup and versioning survive mistakes and attacks.
Cool and Cold are online (instant reads); Archive is offline and needs rehydration.

misconceptions.myth: Premium is always faster for every workload.
misconceptions.reality: Premium suits high transaction, low-latency patterns; large sequential reads may do well on Standard.

architectureDecisions: Tier by access pattern; automate with lifecycle rules.
Redundancy by failure you must survive (zone, region).
Soft delete + versioning everywhere; immutability or vaulted backup for critical data.

walkthrough.subtitle: Pay only for the performance you need, and never lose data — to failures, mistakes or attackers.
learn: Protection: soft delete, versioning, immutability, backup

steps.label: Problem
steps.title: Petabytes, mostly old
body: Storing everything in the fastest tier is expensive, and a single mistake or attack could still wipe it out.

steps.label: Fit
steps.title: Match storage to access
body: Premium block blob for many small fast transactions. Hot for daily use. Cool and Cold for rarely read data (minimum 30/90 days). Archive for data you can wait hours for (minimum 180 days).

steps.label: Automate
steps.title: Lifecycle rules move data for you
body: Rules move blobs to cooler tiers and delete them by age or last access, so cost falls automatically.

steps.label: Durability
steps.title: Survive failures with redundancy
body: ZRS survives a datacenter failure; GZRS also survives a regional disaster. RA- lets you read the secondary.

callout.text: Redundancy also copies deletions and encryption by ransomware — it is not a backup.

steps.label: Protection
steps.title: Survive mistakes and attackers
body: Soft delete and versioning undo deletes and overwrites. Immutability makes data unchangeable for a set time. Vaulted backup keeps a copy outside the account.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Cost, performance, durability
body: Right tier, right copies, right protection.
recap: Soft delete, versioning, WORM, vaulted backup
